headline.purpose: The page h1 only. Appears exactly once.

title.purpose: Section headers (panel h2/h3) - two real sizes, 1.15rem and 1rem, same weight/role.

body.purpose: Prose, but in practice most on-screen text is the compact 0.78-0.95rem end of this range - specs, captions, table cells.

label.purpose: Uppercase eyebrow sub-headers ("MY QUIVER") and group headers - never used for primary content.

shadows.name: ambient-lift
shadows.purpose: The system's single shadow role, used at rest on panels, the search-results dropdown, and the chart tooltip. Dark mode: 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.4).

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single full-width primary CTA ("What should I add?").
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { width: 100%; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; color: #fff; background: #2a78d6; border: none; border-radius: 8px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #184f95; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { background: #dbe4ee; color: #5b6b7c; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Toggle Chip
components.description: Pill-shaped secondary toggle (view-as-table, info panel, interest chips) - aria-pressed drives the active state.
components.css: .ds-toggle-chip { background: #f4f7fb; border: 1px solid #dbe4ee; color: #1c2b3a; font-size: 0.8rem; padding: 0.4rem 0.7rem; border-radius: 999px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-toggle-chip:hover { border-color: #2a78d6; } .ds-toggle-chip[aria-pressed='true'] { background: #2a78d6; border-color: #2a78d6; color: #fff; }

components.name: Quiver Chip
components.description: A removable pill representing one selected ski, with a circular remove button meeting the 24x24 WCAG tap-target minimum.
components.css: .ds-quiver-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.4rem; background: #f4f7fb; border: 1px solid #dbe4ee; border-radius: 999px; padding: 0.35rem 0.4rem 0.35rem 0.85rem; font-size: 0.9rem; color: #1c2b3a; } .ds-quiver-chip-remove { border: none; background: #dbe4ee; color: #1c2b3a; width: 28px; height: 28px; border-radius: 50%; cursor: pointer; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; padding: 0; } .ds-quiver-chip-remove:hover { background: #d03b3b; color: #fff; }

components.name: Search Input
components.description: The recessed (page-background, not panel-white) search field shared by both search boxes in the app.
components.html: <input class="ds-search-input" type="text" placeholder="Search skis by name…" />
components.css: .ds-search-input { width: 100%; padding: 0.65rem 0.85rem; font-size: 1rem; border: 1px solid #dbe4ee; border-radius: 8px; background: #f4f7fb; color: #1c2b3a; } .ds-search-input:focus { outline: 2px solid #2a78d6; outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-search-input:disabled { opacity: 0.6; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Status Card
components.description: Condition card with a tinted background and solid left-border, colored by state (good/warning/critical) - color is always paired with an icon and label, never used alone.
components.html:
✕

components.css: .ds-status-card { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: 0.6rem; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 3px solid transparent; padding: 0.85rem 0.9rem; } .ds-status-card[data-status='critical'] { background: rgba(208,59,59,0.12); border-left-color: #d03b3b; } .ds-status-icon { font-weight: 700; color: #d03b3b; } .ds-status-desc { margin: 0 0 0.2rem; font-size: 0.95rem; font-weight: 600; color: #1c2b3a; } .ds-status-detail { margin: 0; font-size: 0.8rem; color: #5b6b7c; }

components.name: Temperament Gauge
components.description: Signature component: a word + position-on-spectrum widget. Never shows the raw 0-100 score as a bare number - always a phrase headline plus a small secondary value.
components.html: Leans damp/charging(62)
components.css: .ds-gauge { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.3rem; min-width: 110px; color: #1c2b3a; } .ds-gauge-track { position: relative; height: 6px; border-radius: 999px; background: #dbe4ee; } .ds-gauge-divider { position: absolute; top: -2px; bottom: -2px; width: 1px; background: #898781; opacity: 0.6; } .ds-gauge-dot { position: absolute; top: 50%; width: 10px; height: 10px; background: #2a78d6; border: 2px solid #fff; border-radius: 50%; transform: translate(-50%, -50%); } .ds-gauge-caption { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 0.3rem; font-size: 0.8rem; } .ds-gauge-phrase { font-weight: 600; } .ds-gauge-value { opacity: 0.7; font-size: 0.75rem; }

narrative.overview: Quiver Gap Finder reads like flight-deck telemetry, not a marketing page: every number on screen earns its place, and nothing is drawn purely for decoration. There is no hero image, no marketing copy, no custom display typeface - the system font stack does all the work, and visual weight is spent almost entirely on making dense spec data (waist width, weight, turn radius, a derived "temperament" score) scannable rather than on styling for its own sake. Color is treated as a signal, not a decoration: one blue hue carries every interactive and chart-accent role, one orange is reserved for the single most important line on the results panel, and a fixed three-color status scale (good/warning/critical) is never reused for anything but literally reporting a state. This is a quiet, precise system by deliberate choice, not by default or neglect - the restraint itself is the current design's whole personality. It is also explicitly a snapshot of the incumbent system, captured as a baseline ahead of a planned visual overhaul; it documents what is true today, not a target to defend.
keyCharacteristics: Zero imagery, zero display typography - plain system fonts carry the entire type system
One sequential accent hue (blue) for every interactive element and every chart mark; color is never used to distinguish individual items
A fixed, reserved status vocabulary (green/amber/red) that means the same thing everywhere it appears and nowhere else
Flat surfaces with a single soft ambient shadow at rest - no elevation ladder
Every chart ships an accessible table-view twin with identical data

rules.name: The Reserved Signal Rule
rules.body: Status green/amber/red mean exactly one thing - gap/redundant/covered - everywhere they appear, and are never repurposed for decoration or unrelated emphasis, even when a "free" color would be convenient.

rules.name: The Reference Palette Rule
rules.body: Status colors, the chart's sequential blue, and the chart-specific greys trace to a fixed external dataviz reference palette (see README.md), not to this system's own neutral scale - that's why they're warm-toned while the UI's own neutrals are cool blue-grey. Don't re-harmonize them; changing them means redoing the dataviz methodology, not a color-matching pass.

rules.name: The No-Bare-Number Rule
rules.body: The derived 0-100 temperament score is never shown alone as a standalone figure - it always appears as a short phrase plus a position-on-spectrum gauge, with the raw number kept as small secondary detail only.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one shadow in this system. A new component doesn't get a bespoke shadow value - it either uses Ambient Lift or stays flat.

dos: Do pair every status/coverage signal with an icon and a text label, never color alone.
Do give every chart an accessible table-view twin with identical underlying data.
Do design mobile layouts as their own real layout, not a scaled-down desktop canvas.
Do treat touch and hover as genuinely different interaction models.
donts: Don't assign arbitrary per-item color coding on the coverage map.
Don't show the derived temperament score as a bare, standalone number anywhere in the UI.
Don't invent a new shadow value for a new component.
Don't re-harmonize the chart's warm-toned greys to match the UI's cool-toned neutrals.
